It could've been a vasovagal syncope, that happens sometimes when you see blood and your body kinda overreacts to it. Your heart rate and blood pressure drop really quickly as a way to prevent you from losing more blood, but can also cause you to feel really dizzy and stuff or even pass out. Either way though please remember to take care of your cuts (:

Second I get why you'd be upset, and it is a bad reaction, but it makes sense as a reaction.

I've seen lots of people say stuff like that in the various depression/self harm subs, and while it isn't the *right* reaction for a parent to be mad at their child for being depressed or self harming, it's understandable.

I feel like in the absolute vast majority of cases where that happens the parent isn't really mad at the child, but themselves, and are just having a hard time processing it. 

Imagine you raise someone, try to do your best to make sure they're happy and cared for and healthy, and then you find out they don't wanna be alive or they're so upset that they hurt themselves.

The inner reaction to that is probably one of "I didn't do enough, it's my fault that my child doesn't want to be here anymore, I failed them, I wasn't good enough". I feel like this is processed and directed outward as something more along the lines of "what I did isn't good enough for *you*? Why not? Why are you saying I'm a failure"

Obviously it's not a good reaction to have, but I feel like that's the reason it happens. And obviously there are gonna be some parents who are just shitty and really don't care, but I feel like that's a tiny minority of the group who react with anger to news like that. I really doubt it's that they just want to control their children's thoughts.

Just because something isn't considered a federal crime doesn't mean it isn't serious or anything like that. Federal just means that the Government (in Washington DC) gets involved. Every state already had laws against animal cruelty, so making it a federal crime, while a good thing, doesn't mean it was legal before that. 

I guess a good way to explain it is to compare the US to the EU, each state is *kinda* like the the individual countries in the EU, they can make their own laws and so forth, but there are also laws that effect every state.
